sample_unit: HealthBench conversations (50-item subsample for clinician rating)

links.outcome: Same-provider LLM judge leniency effect on apparent model safety ranking
links.effect: Positive same-provider association remained after leniency adjustment (exact permutation p = 0.04; GPT-5.5 ~ +0.10 probability); excluding own-provider judge changed which model over-commits least; Fleiss' kappa 0.65.
links.quote: First, judge choice materially changes apparent safety: inter-judge agreement is only moderate (Fleiss' kappa = 0.65), and after adjusting for each judge's general leniency (vote-level logistic regression), a positive same-provider association remains (exact permutation p = 0.04; GPT-5.5 ~ +0.10 on the probability scale) - large enough to change which model appears to over-commit least once its own-provider judge is excluded.

links.outcome: Agreement of LLM judges with blinded clinician reference on crediting appropriate uncertainty
links.effect: All four LLM judges significantly more lenient than the stricter clinician (credited uncertainty on 66-84% of items vs 52%); judge-vs-consensus kappa 0.20-0.43.
links.quote: Second, LLM judges are more permissive than clinicians on a blinded 50-item subsample: all four are significantly more lenient than the stricter independent clinician (crediting appropriate uncertainty on 66-84% of items vs 52%), and three of four than the author-influenced consensus (Grok directional only; judge-vs-consensus kappa = 0.20-0.43).

links.outcome: Model safety when final user turn is truncated (missing information), knowledge versus calibration
links.effect: MedQA accuracy high with option-order effects within +/-5-point equivalence for three of four models, indicating the safety gap under missing information is calibration, not knowledge.
links.quote: A closed-ended MedQA anchor confirms accuracy is high and option-order effects are within a +/-5-point equivalence region for three of four models, so the safety gap is about calibration, not knowledge.

unlisted_practices: Using LLM-as-judge panels across multiple providers to grade open-ended medical AI safety
Adjusting for judge leniency when evaluating models with LLM judges

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM stress-testing and safety under missing information, specifically testing evaluation practices/guardrails (LLM-as-a-judge panels versus human clinician raters and provider bias in evaluation).

primary.practice: LLM-as-a-judge vs clinician evaluation and judge panel selection
